a:r.a:t: Evolutionary Trees Show the Relationship Between Humans and Chimpanzees

p:cNvPr.descr: An evolutionary tree for progesterone receptors which helps regulate many events in reproduction. The tree has three lineages: the human (far left), the chimpanzee (middle), and the bonobo (right). The node that shows the split between the common ancestor of humans and the common ancestor of chimps is far down to the left, just below the human lineage begins. To the upper right is the node that shows the split between chimps and bonobos. To the right of the line labeled “human”, the locations and changes of amino acids for the progesterone receptor are listed. The amino acid changes are listed with an arrow; they will be described here with the word “to”: 171: G to R; 184: A to V; 204: S to A; 213: G to E; 228: P to A; 359: S to C; 444: P to T; 679: I to V. Below the node for the divergence of humans, there is a single change: 182: G to R. To the upper right, the list of amino acid changes for the chimpanzee are: 535: N to S; 545: A to T; 691: T to S. To the immediate right, the list of changes for the bonobo are: 265: A to T; 267: A to V; 348: A to V. Just below the node for the divergence of the lineages for chimps and bonobos are two changes: 83: D to N and 312: V to M.

p:cNvPr.descr: A diagram shows the homology between human and chimp chromosomes. The top chromosome is human chromosome 2 (labeled above) and consists of two rod-shaped units laid end-to-end. The right unit is slightly shorter than the left. They are off white in color and have several irregular gray bands. Below, the chimpanzee chromosome, labeled below, is actually two: chromosome 2p (left) and chromosome 2q (right). Both are brown with dark gray irregular bands. Chromosome 2p has a long left unit and a short right unit; the reverse is true for chromosome 2q.
